metadata.title: Braxton Berrios - Officially goes to IR
metadata.description: The Giants placed Berrios (foot) on their injured reserve list Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Berrios was already determined to have sustained a season-ending foot injury during Sunday's contest versus the Cardinals, so the move comes as no surprise. His being out could create more opportunities at wide receiver and as a returner for Charlie Jones, who was signed to the Giants' active roster from their practice squad in late September.

metadata.title: Braxton Berrios (leg) to undergo season-ending surgery
metadata.description: Giants WR/returner Braxton Berrios will undergo season-ending surgery for the lower-leg injury he suffered.
metadata.analysis: Berrios was signed to the active roster after the Giants released Odell Beckham Jr.

metadata.title: Braxton Berrios - Undergoing season-ending surgery
metadata.description: Berrios announced Tuesday that he will undergo foot surgery and be out for the rest of the 2026 season, Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Berrios injured his foot during the Giants' Week 4 win over the Cardinals, and the injury is severe enough for him to require season-ending surgery. In Berrios' absence, the Giants will likely turn to Tyrone Tracy, Charlie Jones and Deonte Banks to serve as returners on kickoffs and punts.

metadata.title: Braxton Berrios - Expected to miss time
metadata.description: Giants head coach John Harbaugh confirmed Berrios is dealing with a foot/ankle injury, but a decision has yet to be made regarding whether the wideout will be placed on injured reserve, Paul Schwartz of the New York Post reports.
metadata.analysis: Though Adam Schefter of ESPN reported earlier Monday that Berrios was ticketed for IR, the Giants apparently plan to evaluate the 30-year-old over the next few days before deciding whether or not to deactivate him. Regardless, Berrios appears poised to miss time, which would pave the way for Charlie Jones to replace him as the Giants' primary return man beginning with Sunday's game against the Commanders. Berrios has suited up for each of the Giants' first four games, drawing just one target while seeing the majority of his playing time on special teams.

metadata.title: Braxton Berrios (foot) placed on IR
metadata.description: The Giants placed WR Braxton Berrios on injured reserve.
metadata.analysis: Berrios will miss at least the next four games.

metadata.title: Braxton Berrios - Won't return vs. Arizona
metadata.description: Berrios (foot) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Berrios will not return to Sunday's game after his foot injury was evaluated by medical staff, and the Giants should have an update on the veteran wide receiver shortly once he undergoes more tests. Charlie Jones will handle most of the return duties on punts and kickoffs in Berrios' absence.

metadata.title: Braxton Berrios - Injures foot in Week 4
metadata.description: Berrios (foot) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Evan Barnes of Newsday reports.
metadata.analysis: Berrios was just signed to the active roster off the practice squad Tuesday and worked as both a wideout and a kick returner Sunday prior to getting hurt. He didn't catch his only target and returned two punts for minus-2 yards. Charlie Jones figures to move up a notch in the WR pecking order and serve as New York's prime kick and punt returner if Berrios can't return.

metadata.title: Braxton Berrios signs with Giants' active roster
metadata.description: The Giants signed WR Braxton Berrios to their 53-man roster.
metadata.analysis: Berrios will figure to make an impact on special teams for the Giants.

metadata.title: Braxton Berrios - Appointed to Giants' roster
metadata.description: The Giants signed Berrios off their practice squad Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
metadata.analysis: After failing to win a spot on the Giants' roster coming out of preseason, Berrios re-signed with the organization as a member of the practice squad. The Giants then elevated him from the practice squad ahead of each of their first three games, with Berrios going without a target over 22 snaps on offense but holding a critical role on special teams as the team's kickoff and punt returner. With the Giants releasing Odell Beckham on Tuesday, Berrios will now be awarded a permanent spot on the 53-man roster.

metadata.title: Braxton Berrios - Reverts to Big Blue's practice squad
metadata.description: Berrios reverted to the Giants' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
metadata.analysis: Berrios played five offensive snaps and seven special-teams snaps in the contest, returning two punts for 12 yards and two kicks for 57 yards. The wide receiver has been the primary returner for the Giants through the first three games of the 2026 regular season, but is now out of active roster elevations. If the team wants Berrios to play returner in Sunday's matchup with the Cardinals, they will need to sign the 30-year-old to the active roster.

metadata.title: Braxton Berrios - Elevated for Sunday's game
metadata.description: The Giants elevated Berrios from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: The Giants have elected to expend Berrios' last practice squad elevation, calling upon the wide receiver for three consecutive weeks. The 30-year-old remains the team's primary kick and punt returner, receiving no targets but recording 81 kick-return yards over the past two games. Berrios will need to be signed to the active roster to participate in any more regular-season games for the Giants after Week 3.
